exact_statement: For any finite uniform Boolean signs f,P, let delta=Pr[f=-1]<=1/4, a(h) the full affine-input/output-character minimum influence, Z_P the subspace of constant-derivative directions, and r=codim Z_P=affine dimension of Fourier support(P). Assume every v outside Z_P has centered derivative cost m_P(v)>=4delta (vacuous when r=0). Then a(fP)-a(f)>=a(P)-4delta*r, H(fP)-H(f)<=r, and for every K>=0 the full-affine optimized deficit change is at most r-K[a(P)-4delta*r]. The proof extracts exactly r independent quotient rows from a minimizing full basis of fP, completes by Z_P, and retains the full f basis cost; it never sums dependent parity swaps. This sharpens the degree-only charge r(2^(1-d)-4delta) when P has GF2 degree<=d and 2^(1-d)>=4delta. For P=(-1)^(x1*x2*x3+x1*x4), r=4, min positive centered cost=1/4 and a(P)=5/4; every four-bit point-negative f with delta1/16 gets new charge1/4 versus old charge0 and deficit upper bound-1 at K20. A class-wide raw-root normal form additionally requires I(f)=a(f) and the comparison for every allowed phase. No universally paid original pair or FEI constant is proved.
hypotheses: Finite uniform Boolean signs; normalized Walsh spectrum; H bits; K>=0
delta<=1/4 and ALL nonconstant derivative directions of P have minority>=4delta
Full affine minima include output characters; phase rank is affine spectral dimension, not physical support size
Independent quotient rows selected once; no unused reserve or history bank is created
proof_dependencies: Finite minimum-parity-basis formula and Fourier coset norm conservation, independently reconstructed
Elementary XOR derivative bound and quotient basis completion; self-contained Section2
